newsitem.title: USA: Oldest McDonald's restaurant to reopen.
newsitem.headline: Oldest McDonald's restaurant to reopen.

text.p: McDonald's, the world's largest hamburger chain, has decided to reopen its oldest surviving restaurant, complete with original golden arches, menus and uniforms from 1953.
"This is going to make us really happy and put us on the tourist map," said Joyce Lawrence, the mayor of the Los Angeles suburb of Downey, Friday.

She was reacting to the decision by McDonald's regional vice president Jeff Schwartz to reopen the original red-and-white-tiled hamburger stand in Downey that the company had closed over two years ago because of structural damage caused by the 1994 earthquake.

The 43-year-old building, with its arches and 60-feet-high neon sign of Speedee, the hustling chef, will reopen Dec. 15. In addition, there will be a museum and gift shop next door selling McDonald's memorabilia.

Schwartz began working for McDonald's 28 years ago as a teenage floor-sweeper and burger-flipper in his native Minnesota. He told the Los Angeles Times that when he first saw the Downey stand 10 months ago, he was overcome with nostalgia.
City officials and architectural preservationists had been unhappy with McDonald's decision to close it down.
"We care about its architecture, history and nostalgia," said Mayor Lawrence, who said she remembered hanging out there as a high school student in the late 50s.
The Los Angeles Conservancy called the stand, which opened Aug. 18, 1953, "one of the most influential designs of commercial architecture in the 20th century."
The new restaurant will look the same: arches, slanted glass and bright colours to attract passing motorists. Fifty seats will be added to the present 20 outdoors.
The menu will stress 1950s fare -- hamburgers, fries and milk shakes, with no breakfasts, salads or chicken McNuggets, and the staff will wear white shirts, hats and bolo ties.
